subject.title: Heartbeat: Use ISO 8601 for Current time and separate trigger timestamp

question: Should OpenClaw change the shared cron-style timestamp contract to ISO 8601 and add a separate heartbeat trigger timestamp, or fold this into the broader prompt-cache timestamp redesign?
rationale: The requested behavior is not a narrow bug fix because it changes model-visible prompt semantics across multiple automation and context-refresh paths, and it may require a new wake-runner timestamp contract.

options.title: Define shared contract first
options.body: Choose exact `Current time`, `Reference UTC`, and optional `Heartbeat triggered at` semantics across heartbeat, cron, reset, post-compaction, memory-flush, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Narrow heartbeat-only ISO
options.body: Limit the change to heartbeat prompt bodies and wake-trigger metadata, accepting that shared helper callers may keep a different timestamp shape.

options.title: Fold into prompt-cache redesign
options.body: Track this under the broader timestamp/cache-boundary work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/71973 and close only after that contract resolves the heartbeat case.

recommendation.title: Define shared contract first
recommendation.body: Choose exact `Current time`, `Reference UTC`, and optional `Heartbeat triggered at` semantics across heartbeat, cron, reset, post-compaction, memory-flush, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Takhoffman introduced the heartbeat current-time helper path, making them the strongest code-history routing candidate for the timestamp contract decision.
